summary: A 1930s two-story 14x14 frame cabin on a private Bonner County tree farm, abandoned and in poor shape; visiting needs the family's permission.

facts.status_note: Abandoned and in poor shape. The register says it was in danger of collapse as of 2017, and a 2025 article says one corner was brought down by gunfire. The Forest Lookout Association lists it as standing.

access.note: Private tree farm. Family signs say permission must be obtained before a visit, per the Idaho Fire Lookouts article of September 14, 2025.

visit.trail_note: Walk-in on a road through the tree farm, about 1.5 miles one way per a 2022 writeup. The register says the building is at risk of collapse; do not enter it.

events.note: Built in the 1930s per the register and a 2022 writeup. The year 1930 here stands for the decade; no single year is given.
Register says the structure was in poor shape and in danger of collapse as of 2017
A writeup reported the tree farm and ranch was for sale at about 22 million dollars; walk-in hiking was allowed at the time
Idaho Fire Lookouts article says one corner was brought down by gunfire and that permission is required; the date of the damage is not given

corrections.why: The register's Built field reads 1930's, and the 2022 writeup says built in the 1930s. No single year is given.
None of the sources read gives a height. The register describes a two-story 14x14 design without a height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2022 writeup says walk-in hiking was allowed then. The September 2025 Idaho Fire Lookouts article says permission must be obtained from the family first. The record uses the later permission rule and the story says so.

The Forest Lookout Association lists it as standing. The register says it was in poor shape and in danger of collapse as of 2017, and the 2025 article reports one corner brought down. The story reports it as standing with the damage described.

sources.title: Poirier Tree Farm Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m of 4.3 is not in any source read; recommend removing it. The brief's built year of 1930 is a decade: the register and the 2022 writeup say 1930s, and the event keeps 1930 as a placeholder year. Access conflict: 2022 walk-in allowed vs 2025 permission required; the later rule is used. The FFLA list's standing status is kept with the 2017 poor-shape note. The 2022 sale listing is the most recent sale information found; no later report was located. Private property: the story advises against entering the building. Web searches used: 2. Distinct pages read: 6, one of which (the Keeping Watch entry) gave only coordinates. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the staffing line now says the site does not yet have a documented staffing history (it does not say none exists); the 2022 date and the sign wording now carry their own quotes.
